**Sikhae (Seaweed Soup) – A Simple Korean Recipe** *This is a quick, comforting soup that’s perfect for a light lunch or dinner. It uses common pantry items and takes about 20–30 minutes from start to finish.* --- ### Ingredients | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Dried kelp (wakame)** | 1 cup (about 5 g dried) | Soaks into a few tablespoons of water; you’ll use the soaked kelp only. | | **Water** | 4 cups (960 ml) | Use fresh tap or filtered water. | | **Soy sauce** | 2 Tbsp (30 ml) | Adjust to taste. | | **Sesame oil** | 1 tsp (5 ml) | Adds aroma; optional but recommended. | | **Garlic** | 1 clove, minced | Optional for extra flavor. | | **Salt** | ½ tsp (2.5 g) | Taste‑adjust after adding soy sauce. | | **Optional add‑ins** | | • Thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms
• Diced tofu (firm, cubed)
• Scallions, chopped (for garnish)
• Sesame seeds (sprinkle on top) | --- ### Equipment - Medium saucepan - Measuring spoons - Knife & cutting board (if adding optional veggies) --- ### Instructions 1. **Prep the Kelp** - Rinse the dried kelp under cold running water to remove any grit. - Place it in a bowl with 1 cup of water. Let it soak for 10–15 minutes until it expands and softens. - Drain the kelp, reserving the soaking liquid (you’ll use it later). Cut the kelp into bite‑sized strips if it’s long. 2. **Cook the Base** - In a medium saucepan, pour the 4 cups of fresh water and bring to a gentle boil over medium heat. - Add the minced garlic (if using) and let it simmer for 1 minute to infuse the water. 3. **Add the Kelp** - Stir in the soaked kelp strips. - Reduce the heat to low and let the soup simmer for 5–7 minutes. The kelp will release its umami flavor into the broth. 4. **Season** - Add the soy sauce and sesame oil. Stir well. - Taste the soup; if it needs more saltiness, sprinkle in the ½ tsp of salt. - If you’re using optional add‑ins (mushrooms, tofu), add them now and let everything simmer together for another 3–4 minutes until the veggies are tender. 5. **Finish & Serve** - Turn off the heat. - Ladle the soup into bowls. - Garnish with chopped scallions and a pinch of sesame seeds if desired. - Serve hot, ideally with steamed rice or a side of kimchi. --- ### Tips & Variations - **Flavor Boost:** Add a splash of mirin or a pinch of sugar to balance the salty soy sauce. - **Protein Upgrade:** Replace tofu with diced chicken breast or shrimp for a heartier meal. - **Texture Play:** Toss in thinly sliced carrots or zucchini for crunch. - **Spice Level:** Add a dash of gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes) or a slice of fresh chili for heat. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a simple, nutritious dish that showcases the delicate flavor of seaweed.
